purpose: Improve defensible Calais/Guines historical cartography by investigating actual archival surveys and dated historical maps before upgrading schematic dashed regional envelopes.
priority: P0 - Calais Pale / Guînes actual frontier outline
already_known: SOURCE_REGISTRY.json contains Murphy (2025) for Guînes 1529 laws, and earlier decades' map-dating inventory includes Nicolay and a later 1556 survey. This supplement specifies additional shelfmarks and chain of custody; deduplicate before public adoption.

sources.title: Julian Munby, The Field of Cloth of Gold: Guînes and the Calais Pale Revisited
sources.read_scope: Publisher metadata/abstract and indexed article footnotes; complete article not examined
sources.importance: Scholarly landscape reconstruction addressing 1520 Guînes, mapped frontier sites, historic surveys and later maps; use primary footnotes as archival pointers, not proof of an exact 1520 boundary.

sources.title: Survey of Calais and the Marches (1556), Court of Augmentations Miscellaneous Books
sources.read_scope: Shelfmarks and contents description reported in Munby (2016) footnote 20; archive volumes not inspected
sources.content_pointer: First volume folios 1–277 covers Calais; second volume folios 278–545 concerns much of the rural parishes; described as limits, ways, watercourses, and parish divisions measured by compass.
sources.dating_caution: 1556 is 27–36 years after target 1520–1529; may not describe original boundaries during that earlier decade. Compare with dated 1520s controls, never silently back-date.

sources.title: Historical Calais Pale map: 1876 tracing of earlier map, ref CPL 1414
sources.read_scope: Historical provenance reported by Munby (2016) footnote 19; archival map copy itself not directly examined
sources.provenance: An original map now lost was lent in 1868 for a tracing; the extant 1876 copy was made from that tracing by J.-A. Cottel. See S. Curveiller (2008) for historical background.
sources.dating_caution: Date and precision of the lost original must be established before any 1520–1529 georeferencing; copying in 1876 is not proof of measured Tudor-period borders.

sources.title: Stéphane Curveiller, Un document exceptionnel: une carte du Calaisis sous la domination anglaise de 1346 à 1558
sources.publication: Le prince, l'argent, les hommes au Moyen Âge (Presses universitaires de Rennes), 2008, pp. 559–570
sources.read_scope: Bibliographic title verified via scholarly citation and institutional record; full book chapter blocked by publisher bot protection
sources.importance: Historical-map provenance and treatment of political Calais geography; verify archival source date and cartographic meaning before digitization.

sources.title: Les fortifications anglaises de Guînes au XVIe siècle: 1541 fortified town plans
sources.publisher: Publications de l’Institut de recherches historiques du Septentrion / OpenEdition
sources.read_scope: Indexed historical-plan image and publisher entry, full article not directly accessible
sources.dating_caution: 1541 fortification design postdates 1529 and follows 1530s rebuilding; useful as retrospective archaeological context, not to draw 1520s fortress walls or territorial extent.

sources.title: Neil Murphy, Tudor England's French Frontier: The Laws of Guînes (1529) and the Defence of the Calais Pale
sources.publisher: Routledge, Borders and Boundaries: Historical Perspectives, 2025
sources.read_scope: University research portal full abstract and bibliographic metadata; complete chapter under embargo, not read
sources.importance: 1525 commission and 1529 legal settlement policies provide context for disputed lands; does not prove enforcement totals or a historically surveyed frontier line.

action_steps.description: Request/locate archival descriptions and digitized accessible originals of TNA E315/371, E315/372. Create place names / measurements / dating table with folio citations. First verify provenance and 1556 dating; do not back-date geometry.
Locate Pas-de-Calais archive CPL 1414 and Curveiller 2008 discussion; determine dating of lost original, copy stages, scale, place names, and reuse rights.
Use Munby 2016 to isolate specifically 1520-year fort/site evidence; separate town/castle footprints from border administrative bounds; compare to Murphy 2025 policy evidence.

Cross-check any proposed boundary segments against 1520–1529 contemporaneous rentals, jurisdiction, military garrison, tax rolls or dated statutes. Assign confirmed/potential/disputed by segment; trace modern-to-early Tudor toponyms.

Only once independently checked, output GeoJSON with metadata archival_call_number, folio, survey_date, applicable_year_from/to, control_class, geometry_method, geometry_confidence, rights. All inferred stretches should be dashed, area calculations prohibited.

no_false_claims: Not personally read or digitally reproduced the original TNA manuscripts or historic maps during this investigation.
Neither 1556 TNA survey nor 1541 Guînes fortress plans establishes an exact 1520–1529 control border.
A 19th-century tracing of a lost map requires original dating and archive confirmation.
Guînes 1529 policy restrictions prove legislative intent, not number of deportees, exact settler land grants, or territorial gain.
